# Greedy Line Wrapping with Even Word Spacing

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/text-justification)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

You receive a body of text along with a maximum line width measured in columns. Arrange the words of the text into lines so that no line exceeds that width and the total number of lines is as small as it can be.

Within each line, distribute the space characters between adjacent words so that the gaps are as close to equal in size as possible.

The last line is an exception: it should not be justified in this way.

## Examples

**Example 1**

```text
Input:
16
This is an example of text justification.
Output:
3
|This    is    an|
|example  of text|
|justification.  |
```

**Example 2**

```text
Input:
16
What must be acknowledgment shall be
Output:
3
|What   must   be|
|acknowledgment  |
|shall be        |
```

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Separate the problem into two steps: first decide which words go on each line, then decide how to place spaces on that line.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Pack words greedily while the line fits, then divide the leftover spaces among the gaps, giving extra spaces to the leftmost gaps when they do not split evenly.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Handle a line with a single word and the last line, which are left-aligned with single spaces and padded on the right.

</details>
